neighbours.label: An emotionally evaluative adjective in predicate position, after a copula or 'looking / can be / has been' ('the future was looking bleak', 'can be utterly maddening', 'which is comforting'); the same adjective placed before a noun, and neutral predicate adjectives, stay quiet
fire: For the families still waiting for news, the long silence has been agonizing.
Her habit of changing the plan at the last minute can be utterly infuriating.
There is a steadiness in his letters which is deeply reassuring.
By late October the outlook for the harvest was looking grim.
The weeks after the diagnosis have been frightening for all of us.
His slow, careful way of answering every question can be quite exasperating.
The smell of bread in the old kitchen is strangely consoling.
For the crew stranded on the ice, the waiting was becoming unbearable.
quiet: For the families still waiting for news, the long silence has been unbroken.
Her habit of changing the plan at the last minute can be easily explained.
There is a watermark in his letters which is barely visible.
By late October the grim outlook for the harvest was widely reported.
The frightening weeks after the diagnosis were followed by a calm spring.
His slow, careful way of answering every question can be quite useful.
The smell of bread in the old kitchen is mostly yeast.
For the crew stranded on the ice, the unbearable waiting ended on Tuesday.

notes: Card flags the gate-closed regime (91% '-x- echo') and the pole is weak (max 6.41); top examples are 'looking bleak', 'utterly maddening', 'which is comforting', 'have been terrifying'. Probes: maddening 0.61, comforting 0.58, terrifying 0.36, bleak 0.31, 'The news was devastating.' 0.21; 'looking different' 0.04, 'wooden and quite old' 0.03, attributive 'the bleak landscape' 0.06.
